question: Show me how to take Punctual Pros nationwide
html:
Taking Punctual Pros nationwide

Follow the Smith + Howard growth plan in four phases. First densify Central PA, then repeat the Horvath deal across the Mid-Atlantic, then build an I-81/I-95 hub, and finally consolidate inside the Authority Brands system. The model takes run-rate revenue from ~$24M to ~$100M in about three years (est.) (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Starting point and template

  • Punctual Pros today: ~$22M est. FY2025 revenue, 25 Authority Brands territories, and 248 core Central-PA zips with ~1.0M housing units. It has one out-of-state add-on, Horvath on the Jersey Shore (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • Smith + Howard precedent: in ~3.7 years it grew from ~100 professionals in one Atlanta office to ~800 professionals, 11 locations, nine acquisitions and ~4x revenue. It sold to TPG Growth in August 2026 (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Four expansion phases

  • Phase 1 (months 0-12): densify the core and 261 Tier-1 adjacent zips (176 PA, 85 MD). Close 1-2 tuck-ins from the 61-company screen.
  • Phase 2 (months 9-24): repeat Horvath across PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY. There are 54 mapped Authority territories not yet owned, and 17 PE sponsors are chasing the same founders.
  • Phase 3 (months 18-36): build a Mid-Atlantic hub covering Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh.
  • Phase 4: become the national consolidator across 1,066 One Hour, Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky outlets ($831M reported revenue). Punctual Pros holds ~2.3% of that today.

# Taking Punctual Pros nationwide

Follow the Smith + Howard growth plan in four phases. First densify Central PA, then repeat the Horvath deal across the Mid-Atlantic, then build an I-81/I-95 hub, and finally consolidate inside the Authority Brands system. The model takes run-rate revenue from ~$24M to ~$100M in about three years (est.) (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## Starting point and template

- **Punctual Pros today:** ~$22M est. FY2025 revenue, 25 Authority Brands territories, and 248 core Central-PA zips with ~1.0M housing units. It has one out-of-state add-on, Horvath on the Jersey Shore (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- **Smith + Howard precedent:** in ~3.7 years it grew from ~100 professionals in one Atlanta office to ~800 professionals, 11 locations, nine acquisitions and ~4x revenue. It sold to TPG Growth in August 2026 (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## Four expansion phases

- **Phase 1 (months 0-12):** densify the core and 261 Tier-1 adjacent zips (176 PA, 85 MD). Close 1-2 tuck-ins from the 61-company screen.
- **Phase 2 (months 9-24):** repeat Horvath across PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY. There are 54 mapped Authority territories not yet owned, and 17 PE sponsors are chasing the same founders.
- **Phase 3 (months 18-36):** build a Mid-Atlantic hub covering Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh.
- **Phase 4:** become the national consolidator across 1,066 One Hour, Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky outlets ($831M reported revenue). Punctual Pros holds ~2.3% of that today.

## Modelled roadmap (all est.)

| Month | Revenue | EBITDA | Technicians | Territories | Members |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | $24M | $2.9M | 85 | 25 | 6,500 |
| 12 | $38M | $5.3M | 135 | 32 | 11,000 |
| 24 | $65M | $9.8M | 230 | 44 | 20,000 |
| 36 | $100M | $16.0M | 350 | 58 | 32,000 |

Source: Punctual Pros nationwide plan. All rows are labelled assumptions.

## First add-on targets

- **Lancaster Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electrical** (fit 84): four trades, 5 miles from headquarters.
- **West Chester tri-brand, Ron Williams group** (fit 82): the same owner is reported for Delmarva, so this could be a two-territory deal.
- **C&C Air Conditioning** (fit 82): Jersey Shore, ~65 employees.
- **Zimmerman and PHE South Jersey** (fit 80 each).
- **Data gap:** revenue and headcount are often missing because ZoomInfo enrichment was unavailable (Punctual Pros add-on targets).

## Lessons from other sponsors

- **Sequence that worked:** sponsors that sold for more followed a common order (Home-services company case studies):
  - hire an integrator COO early;
  - add roughly one company per quarter;
  - put every brand on one system;
  - build memberships (Champions reached ~83 members per technician and sold at a reported ~18.5x);
  - own the technician pipeline.
- **Failure pattern:** Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint grew brand count faster than they integrated.
- **AI layer:** a 24/7 voice dispatcher (ServiceTitan reports 70% booking) and missed-call text-back drive the organic lift assumed in Phase 1 (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- **Financing:** the context is truncated. Confirming capacity needs the current credit agreement and add-on purchase multiples.

## Next actions

1. Recruit an integrator COO before closing the second tuck-in.
2. Open conversations with Lancaster Plumbing and the Ron Williams group. Request trailing financials to fill the revenue gaps.
3. Set a membership-per-technician KPI against the Champions benchmark, starting at ~76 (est.).
4. Build an acquisition financing model to test whether the month-36 roadmap can be funded.
